vs_stocks_note: The 364-day T-bill now yields 15.85% against August inflation of 15.39%. The risk-free return barely beats inflation. Falling T-bill yields (as now) usually make equities look more attractive, since the 'safe' alternative pays less. Rising yields do the opposite.

tax.note: FIRS directive of October 2025: 10% withholding tax deducted at source on T-bill interest; FGN bond interest remains exempt. Investors receive tax credits for amounts withheld.
sources: FIRS public notice via TheCable Oct 2025
FIRS clarification via The Sun Oct 2025

auction_calendar.run_by: CBN, on behalf of the Federal Government/DMO
auction_calendar.caveat: Follows the bi-weekly Wednesday pattern; the CBN occasionally shifts dates around holidays.

savings_bond_calendar.pattern: Usually opens the first Monday of the month, closes Friday, settles the following Wednesday.
savings_bond_calendar.caveat: Expected dates; confirmed when the DMO publishes the monthly circular.

auction_notes.text: Demand stayed strong: N1.032tn bid for N450bn offered (2.3x cover), but the CBN allotted only N269.06bn. The 364-day stop rate edged up 5bps to 15.90%, a pause in the easing run that began after September's 350bp MPR cut to 23.00%. (CBN via Nairametrics/Punch)
The 364-day stop rate fell 4bps to 15.85%, extending the decline since the CBN cut the MPR to 23.00% in September. The 91-day and 182-day rates held steady.

fgn_bond_curve.source: AIICO Capital investor note via dmarketforces
fgn_bond_curve.read: The curve slopes down after 7 years: 20-year paper yields 14.69%, below the 10-year at 16.43%. Investors accept less for longer dates when they expect rates to fall over time.
